applicationPortal.value: Apply to UNT Graduate Admissions through UNT Graduate CAS first. After applying to UNT, applicants receive a UNT Student ID number by email; the UNT Admissions Office processes the Student ID number two to three business days after application submission. Applicants cannot submit the College of Music application until they receive the Student ID number. Complete the College of Music application through Acceptd, which opens September 1 each year. The College of Music application is the application for audition, admission, and music merit awards. Applicants select Graduate Degrees as level, select the appropriate area and program, and submit the music application. For MM and DMA Performance, UNT lists required online music application materials as resume or curriculum vitae, repertoire list for the last five years, example of scholarly writing or statement of personal interest, and three letters of recommendation. Candidates for Master's and Doctoral Performance programs must pass an audition on the required repertoire for their instrument or voice. UNT states it no longer requires the GRE or UNT Graduate Writing Exam; admission decisions are made holistically based on the UNT application, College of Music application and supplemental materials, interview or audition, and other materials.

auditionRequirements.value: Applicants for admission to the MM or DMA degree programs in performance must pass an admission audition before a faculty panel. Live auditions are preferred for both music admission and award consideration. Auditions occur as either live audition/interview on campus in Denton or final video audition for applicants who cannot attend in person and/or who apply after live auditions are full and closed. Following review of a video audition, faculty may require an interview or virtual audition if additional information is needed. A screening, meaning a preliminary video audition, is required for live audition consideration. All graduate areas require screening. Screening videos and final audition videos must include both audio and video, be unedited and without artificial audio enhancement, and be recorded within the past six months. Applicants should check the quality and playability of videos before upload. Unless the instrument specifically indicates otherwise, all classical instrumental applicants are expected to audition without accompaniment. For Piano, all graduate piano applicants must submit a video screening recording to determine advancement in the audition process; the screening repertoire is the same as the live audition repertoire. Both on-campus and off-campus auditions are scheduled in January and February each year. A live audition is recommended for entering graduate performance students. All movements of a multi-movement work should be submitted in one continuous take. Piano English-proficiency note: to be scheduled for an audition or have a final video audition reviewed, all MM and DMA piano applicants must submit proof of UNT English Language Proficiency, either a standardized language test or official transcript of a U.S. degree completed or in progress; no admission or music award offer can be made until UNT English Language Proficiency is demonstrated. All new MM and DMA students who do not hold a BM in Performance from UNT must take the Graduate Piano Literature Examination during new graduate orientation.

deadlines.value: September 1: College of Music application opens each year. November 1: deadline to be considered for a live audition/interview on the December audition date for Fall admission according to the College of Music deadline page. December 1: preference deadline for January or February live audition/interview dates according to the College of Music deadline page. February 15: final deadline to submit the music application and video auditions for most audition areas. February 1: final deadline to submit video auditions/portfolios for Piano, Graduate Voice, Jazz Studies, Commercial Music, Critical Studies, and Electronics. Mid-March: applicants are notified of admission results by email or through Acceptd. April 15: admitted music majors are asked to accept or decline the offer of admission by April 15 each year. Program note: the College of Music Graduate Requirements page lists in-person audition/interview dates as Friday, December 5, 2025; Saturday, January 31, 2026; Saturday, February 7, 2026; Friday, February 20, 2026 for graduate applicants in Ethnomusicology, Musicology, Music Education, Music Theory, Percussion, Piano, Strings, Voice, and DMA Jazz only; and Saturday, February 28, 2026, with Graduate Voice auditions not available on that date. Program note: as of 2026-05-25, UNT's deadline page heading says Spring/Fall 2027 admission, but the posted audition-date list still shows 2025-2026 dates; applicants should confirm the updated audition calendar with the College of Music before relying on exact audition dates.

englishScores.value: Minimum scores: TOEFL iBT 79 for exams taken before January 21, 2026. Minimum scores: TOEFL iBT 4 for exams taken on or after January 21, 2026. Minimum scores: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall band. Minimum scores: PTE 53. Minimum scores: Duolingo English Test 100. Minimum scores: Michigan English Test 4-skill exam section scores of 54. Minimum scores: Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency C1. Notes: TOEFL iBT excludes MyBest scores. Notes: submit TOEFL scores electronically through ETS using school code 6481. Notes: SAT 1 with 560 or higher on both Critical Reading and Writing and ACT English 21 or higher are also listed under high school/secondary school exam options. Timing: English proficiency tests must be taken within two years prior to applying, and test scores expire after two years. Notes: expired scores are accepted for students who have been continuously enrolled at a college or university in the U.S. since before the scores expired, but students must submit official score reports. Exemptions: ELP may be demonstrated through citizenship in an approved English-speaking country, qualifying high school/secondary school or college/university study in an approved country, completion of Level 6 at UNT's Intensive English Language Institute, or other listed exams/coursework. Program note: for Piano, proof of UNT English Language Proficiency is required before an MM or DMA applicant can be scheduled for an audition or have a final video audition reviewed, and no admission or music award offer can be made until this information is provided.

auditionRequirements.value: To be considered for a live audition, Collaborative Piano applicants must submit a completed online application that includes a comprehensive repertoire list for all genres. The audition will not be scheduled until all materials are received. Collaborative piano performance applicants submit screening recordings in the categories listed by UNT. At the beginning of the screening recording, applicants should state their name and degree sought or embed that information in the video itself. Applicants should check both quality and playability before upload. Recordings should be unedited, reflect one take as in live performance, and be no more than one year old at the time of submission. Recordings are to be submitted on or before December 1 and are reviewed by the collaborative piano faculty. Applicants applying for live audition are notified before the end of December of the screening result. UNT provides partners for all in-person auditions, and the listed live-audition repertoire is required. Live audition is strongly recommended, but final audition by recording is allowed. If auditioning via recording, applicants should state at the beginning of the recordings their name, degree and major sought, and that the recording is the final audition. UNT cannot provide partners for recorded auditions. Candidates auditioning by recording may be requested to interview via Zoom. Collaborative Piano English-proficiency note: because of the demands of the program and the importance of effective communication, all MM and DMA applicants must submit proof of English Language Proficiency, either a standardized language test or an official transcript of a U.S. degree completed or in progress, before they can be scheduled for a live audition. No admission or music award offer can be made until this information is provided. Music awards are not available for students who choose to attend IELI. Questions should be directed to Professor Elvia Puccinelli at least two weeks before any deadlines.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: Master's Level screening materials include 15-30 minutes of instrumental duo repertoire. Prescreening repertoire: Master's Level screening materials include 10-20 minutes of vocal repertoire representing several styles and languages. Prescreening repertoire: Master's Level screening materials include one solo work, memorized, 5-10 minutes in length. Prescreening repertoire: Master's Level screening materials include a video in which the applicant introduces themself and discusses collaborative experience and professional goals. Prescreening repertoire: Optional videos of coaching, conducting, or teaching are welcome. Prescreening repertoire: Additional performance recordings, including individual selections, recital sets or complete performances, may be submitted as supplementary material to give the fullest picture of the applicant's artistry and accomplishments. Final audition repertoire: Beethoven Cello Sonata Op. 69 in A major, first movement, until recapitulation. Final audition repertoire: Strauss Allerseelen in E-flat. Final audition repertoire: Faure Mandoline in A-flat. Final audition repertoire: Sing and play Barber The Daisies in any key, singing in any octave preferred by the applicant. Final audition repertoire: One solo work, memorized, 5-10 minutes in length. Final audition repertoire: Sightreading. Final audition repertoire: Discussion of past work and future goals. Additional repertoire notes: for final audition by recording, the live audition repertoire must be included as part of the total recordings submitted.
